pathway.title: Vestis Corp — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Vestis has reduced reported leverage on every measure while its top line has contracted. Company-reported net leverage moved from 4.72x at October 3, 2025 to 4.83x at January 2, 2026, 4.47x at April 3, 2026 and 4.10x at July 3, 2026, and the leverage on the financial handoff's basis (company Adjusted EBITDA, principal debt plus finance leases) moved from 5.19x to 4.33x for total debt and from 5.07x to 4.13x for net debt over the same dates [CP-1, Chart data: leverage]. The mechanism is both a smaller numerator (principal debt of USD 1,097.5 million at July 3, 2026 after repayments) and a larger denominator, because trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 257,425 thousand to USD 290,437 thousand. For creditors this is genuine progress, categorised as Documentary Fact for the reported ratios and Analyst Interpretation for the reading that it reflects operations rather than only repayment.

The covenant cushion is adequate today and narrows on a known schedule. At July 3, 2026 the reported ratio of 4.10x sat 0.90x below the 5.00x maximum, equal to an EBITDA cushion of USD 52,961 thousand or 18.0% of covenant EBITDA; holding July 3, 2026 net debt constant, the same cushion falls to USD 40,272 thousand (13.7%) at 4.75x and USD 26,174 thousand (8.9%) at 4.50x [CP-1, Calculation steps]. Any shortfall in plan savings or a rise in net debt therefore bites first at the 4.50x test from the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The calculation is static and company-reported; it is not a forecast. The minimum interest cover covenant of 2.00x looks distant on an indicative basis (3.35x on covenant EBITDA over interest expense, net), but the executed definition is not supplied and the company does not print the ratio.

Business risk is moderate: the revenue base is recurring but shrinking. About 95% of fiscal 2025 revenue was recurring rental under multi-year contracts, spread over more than 300,000 accounts with the ten largest customers under 10% of revenue [CP-1A, Company and operating model]. Against that, nine month revenue fell 1.9%, net volumes fell 2.0%, partly through a deliberate exit of unprofitable business, and fiscal 2025 included the loss of a national account [CP-1, Financial base view; CP-1A, Credit translations]. The mechanism is operating leverage: with a fixed plant and route network, falling volume compresses margin unless cost is removed at least as fast, so the recovery in earnings depends on the transformation plan and on pricing, both of which management reports as working through the third quarter.

The transformation plan carries the earnings case and is mostly a management claim. Management targets annual savings of at least USD 75 million by the end of fiscal 2026 and reports roughly USD 30 million realised through the third quarter, while the estimated plan cost has risen from a range of USD 25 million to USD 30 million in the 10-K to a range of USD 35 million to USD 40 million in the latest 10-Q [CP-1A, Conflicts and inherited items]. Category: Management Language for the savings, Documentary Fact for the cost estimate change. For creditors the implication is that covenant headroom is partly a function of adjustments and savings that have not been independently verified, and execution risk includes service disruption and customer attrition.

Liquidity is adequate and bank maturities are distant. Liquidity of USD 351.8 million at July 3, 2026 comprised USD 294.2 million of revolver availability and USD 57.7 million of cash, with no revolver borrowings; the term loans mature in fiscal 2028 (USD 436.0 million) and fiscal 2031 (USD 661.5 million) [CP-1, Chart data: liquidity and debt maturities]. The revolver commitment of USD 300 million also matures in September 2028, so the first bank refinancing is just under two years away, not immediate.

The receivables securitization is the nearest funding event and a source of cash flow flattery. The USD 250 million facility is scheduled to terminate on August 2, 2027, and USD 212.3 million of receivables had been sold and derecognized at July 3, 2026, up USD 9.8 million since October 3, 2025 [CP-1, Calculation steps]. The mechanism is that the sold balance is not debt on the balance sheet; if the facility ended without replacement, receivables would return to the balance sheet and be funded from cash and the revolver, the credit agreement caps such facilities at USD 250 million, and the company's own net debt table does not include the sold balance. How the covenant counts the sold balance is unresolved: adding it to company net debt at July 3, 2026 gives 4.82x against the 5.00x maximum, and the same exercise at October 3, 2025 gives 5.45x, above the maximum then in force although the company reported compliance, which suggests the covenant does not count the whole balance on that basis. Category: Analyst Interpretation resting on an illustrative calculation, with the executed definition Not supplied.

Cash flow quality improved but should be read with care. Nine month operating cash flow was USD 160,873 thousand against USD 33,302 thousand a year earlier, and trailing twelve month free cash flow of USD 136,411 thousand was 47.0% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1, Calculation steps]. Of the USD 127,571 thousand increase, the accepted financial handoff attributes USD 79.0 million to changes in operating assets and liabilities, while receivables sold rose by USD 9.8 million and USD 34,256 thousand of plan cash costs were absorbed in operating cash flow. Implication: free cash flow is real but includes working capital release that is unlikely to repeat at the same scale, and dividends and buybacks are restricted until conditions are met, so cash is going to debt service rather than shareholders.

Governance looks creditor-neutral with monitoring items. No sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or creditor-adverse action is documented, dividends are restricted, and the company reports its covenant ratio and liquidity each quarter; offsetting this, the chief financial officer role is interim, securities class actions alleging misleading disclosure are in discovery, and tax-free spin-off restrictions and indemnification obligations to Aramark remain unquantified [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Category: Documentary Fact for the events, Insufficient Information for the exposures.

cells.text: Provider of uniform rentals and workplace supplies across the United States and Canada: "a leading provider of uniform rentals and workplace supplies across the United States and Canada"
Narrow product scope in one industry; revenue ties to employment and workplace activity, so cash flow is exposed to labour-market and manufacturing cycles.
Recurring rental revenue is most of the business: "Revenue from our recurring rental business comprised 95% of total revenue, with 5% from direct sales."
Recurring weekly billing gives visibility and cash conversion; the 5% direct sales line is lumpier and carried a national account loss.
"The vast majority of our customers are served under multi-year contracts." Early termination without cause carries specified exit costs.
Contract terms are not supplied, so renewal timing and pricing resets cannot be tested; visibility is real but unquantified.
"We deliver to over 300,000 customer accounts"; the ten largest customers are "less than 10% of total revenue in fiscal year 2025".
No single-customer concentration, which limits event risk; a broad base spreads credit loss but shows up as receivables and bad debt, which the company reserved against in fiscal 2025 (10-K page:68).
United States 91% and Canada 9% of fiscal 2025 revenue; two reportable segments.
Canada is small, so foreign exchange is secondary to US volume and cost trends.
Over 325 facilities and over 3,300 routes; "Approximately 60% of our uniforms and linens are manufactured in our two manufacturing plants in Mexico."
Concentrated manufacturing in Mexico exposes cost of services to tariffs and trade policy, which the company lists as a risk; sensitivity is not quantified (Insufficient Information for tariff cost).
Competitors of size are named as Cintas and UniFirst; the company says it is "the second largest provider in our industry".
Competitive pricing and service quality drive customer retention, and rivals can target accounts during the company's service and volume reset.
Q3 FY2026 net volumes were lower, "partially offset by strategic pricing improvements"; the release says Revenue Per Pound rose 3% in the quarter.
Price and mix are replacing volume; if price gains reverse or volume loss accelerates, revenue and operating leverage weaken. Pounds processed are management estimates.

Significant cost inputs are labour, merchandise in service, plant operating costs and delivery; elevated energy prices have had an impact (Q3 10-Q page:41). Over 200 collective bargaining agreements cover part of the workforce (10-K page:32).
Labour and energy are the main margin pressures, and unionisation limits speed of restructuring; wage and fuel inflation compress margin if not repriced.
Cash purchases of property and equipment plus new vehicle finance leases make up investment in capital assets (Q3 release page:17).
Fleet is partly lease-financed, so debt-like claims sit outside the term loans (see the financial handoff for balances).
Receivables are partly sold through the securitization facility; working capital improvement and higher use of the facility helped operating cash flow (Q3 10-Q page:51).
Cash flow quality depends on the facility continuing; it is scheduled to terminate August 2, 2027, which is a refinancing event (Q3 10-Q page:50).
Three priorities: Commercial Excellence, Operational Excellence, Asset and Network Optimization; "annual operating cost savings of at least $75 million by the end of fiscal 2026".
Savings are the main driver of the recovery in covenant EBITDA; they are unaudited and execution risk, customer attrition from service disruption and cash restructuring costs are real.

runs.text: Strengths. First, recurring revenue and breadth: recurring weekly rental is about 95% of revenue, with no meaningful customer concentration, which supports revenue visibility and limits event risk [Documentary Fact, from the business handoff]. Second, deleveraging with real cash generation: principal debt is down USD 71.0 million since October 3, 2025 and trailing free cash flow of USD 136,411 thousand funded it, with the revolver undrawn [Documentary Fact for the debt and cash flow, from the financial handoff]. Third, liquidity and maturity profile: liquidity of USD 351.8 million and no bank maturity until fiscal 2028 give time to execute the plan [Documentary Fact]. Fourth, a single secured bank facility with no junior debt in the sources: all funded borrowings sit in one credit agreement (finance leases and the receivables facility sit alongside it) guaranteed by the company and substantially all wholly-owned domestic material subsidiaries and secured on substantially all tangible assets, which keeps the structure simple and the covenant package, once read in full, central to monitoring [Documentary Fact; legal capacity Not supplied]. Fifth, improving margins: trailing Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.8% against 9.4% for fiscal 2025 on the company's non-GAAP definition [Management Language, company-defined].

Weaknesses. First, leverage remains high and the covenant tightens: reported net leverage of 4.10x is below the 5.00x maximum, but the maximum falls to 4.50x from the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which leaves a smaller cushion at constant net debt [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the cushion]. Second, a shrinking top line: revenue down 1.9% and volume down 2.0% over nine months mean earnings recovery is cost-led [Documentary Fact]. Third, dependence on a management-quantified plan whose cost estimate has risen and whose savings are unaudited [Management Language]. Fourth, off-balance-sheet receivables funding with a defined end date and unresolved covenant treatment [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the covenant]. Fifth, definition risk: two company figures for fiscal 2025 Adjusted EBITDA differ, and covenant EBITDA includes adjustments the company defines [Documentary Fact]. Sixth, leadership and legal overhang: an interim chief financial officer and pending securities class actions [Documentary Fact; exposure Insufficient Information]. Seventh, supply chain concentration: about 60% of uniforms and linens are made in two plants in Mexico, with tariff sensitivity not quantified [Documentary Fact; sensitivity Insufficient Information].

runs.text: The transaction history in the sources is the separation from Aramark and the financings around it; there is no sponsor transaction, acquisition or disposal of size, and no new debt issue in fiscal 2026 to the cutoff. On September 29, 2023 the company and certain subsidiaries entered into a senior secured credit agreement, and the separation was completed on September 30, 2023 by a distribution of Vestis shares to Aramark holders at one Vestis share for every two Aramark shares; the company used about 1,457 million of term loan proceeds to transfer cash to Aramark (10-K page:112, page:145). The agreement was amended on February 22, 2024 to refinance the original 800 million term loan A-1 with an 800 million term loan B-1 due February 2031, and on May 1, 2025 to raise the maximum net leverage ratio in stages, grant a one-time 15 million bad debt adjustment to covenant EBITDA, cap receivables facilities at 250 million and restrict dividends and share repurchases (10-K page:113, page:115). A three-year 250 million accounts receivable securitization was put in place on August 2, 2024 (10-K page:146). Use of proceeds on the securitization was repayment of part of the term loans (Q3 10-Q page:50). In fiscal 2026 the sources show only repayments of principal, with no new instrument. Liquidity effect and covenant terms are in the earlier financial handoff and are company-reported; the executed amendments are not supplied. The company also sold its equity stake in Aramark Uniform Services Japan Corporation in the first quarter of fiscal 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:15). Status of every item above: completed; none is draft or pending.

fields.value: Overall view: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. The effective source set is the three filed periodic reports for fiscal 2026, the filed annual report for fiscal 2025 and the three earnings releases that the company furnished with them. Together they give located statements, debt and covenant notes, liquidity tables and operating narrative for every consumer. The owner of each downstream method can perform its work, with bounded gaps that are listed below and carried into the consumer assessments. No source is blocked, no critical identity boundary is unresolved, and no source conflict was found between the filings and the releases on the figures checked for location. Source readiness here is not a statement that downstream analysis is complete, and no figure was normalized or reconciled in this module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that the governing financing documents are not in the pack: the Credit Agreement, its first and second amendments and the receivables facility documents are exhibits listed by reference only (10-K page:151 and page:152), so covenant levels, step-downs and definitions come from the company's own note and MD&A summaries. A second limitation is that the leverage ratio the company reports is its own non-GAAP presentation and the credit agreement definition, as summarized in the 10-Q, also counts advances under any receivables facility; how the receivables facility enters the reported ratio is not stated in the sources (see Version relationships and conflicts). Mechanism: when the executed definition cannot be read, headroom to the maintenance test depends on management's summary and its adjustments, so the consequence is that covenant headroom and any stress of it must be labelled as company-reported and unverified downstream.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Vestis Corp entered fiscal 2026 with company-reported net leverage of 4.72x against a 5.25x maximum, and has since de-levered through earnings recovery and debt paydown rather than growth. Revenue is still falling: nine month revenue was $1,984.5 million, down 1.9% on the prior year, with net volumes down 2.0% and the decline attributed in part to a deliberate exit of unprofitable volume under the transformation plan (Q3 10-Q page:46). Earnings are recovering from cost action: nine month operating income rose from 46,790 to 80,605 (US$ thousands), while nine month SG&A fell 44.0 million, of which a 15 million bad debt charge in Q2 fiscal 2025 explains part (Q3 10-Q page:46). Company Adjusted EBITDA on a trailing twelve month basis rose from 257,425 at fiscal 2025 year end to 290,437 at July 3, 2026 (US$ thousands, release page:14).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt is entirely secured bank debt plus finance leases: term loan A-2 of 436,000 due September 2028 and term loan B-1 of 661,500 due February 2031 (US$ thousands), with the 300 million revolver undrawn. Principal debt fell by 71.0 million from fiscal 2025 year end to July 3, 2026 (calculated below). Cash interest paid on principal debt was 55.7 million for nine months against 64.7 million a year earlier (Q3 10-Q page:16), consistent with lower borrowings and a lower weighted-average rate of 6.23% against 6.80% (Q3 10-Q page:21).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the metrics used for the charts below (company Adjusted EBITDA, principal debt plus finance leases), total debt over trailing EBITDA moved from 5.19x to 4.33x and net debt over trailing EBITDA from 5.07x to 4.13x between fiscal 2025 year end and July 3, 2026. The company's own covenant ratio, which uses covenant Adjusted EBITDA and adds letters of credit, moved from 4.72x to 4.10x against a maximum of 5.25x stepping to 5.00x (release page:16, Q3 10-Q page:20). Liquidity at July 3, 2026 was 351.8 million, made of 294.2 million of revolver availability and 57.7 million of cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three issues keep the view at medium confidence. First, the executed credit agreement is not in the pack, so the covenant definition is read from summaries, and those summaries define covenant indebtedness to include advances under any receivables facility (Q3 10-Q page:52) while the company's net debt table has no such line (release page:16); the sold receivables balance was 212.3 million at July 3, 2026. Second, the maximum leverage ratio steps down to 4.75x for the quarter ending October 2, 2026 and 4.50x from the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:20), so today's headroom is not permanent. Third, the receivables facility is scheduled to terminate on August 2, 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:50); because the sold balance is off balance sheet, its end would draw on liquidity. The credit read-through is a deleveraging credit with adequate near-term liquidity and no bank maturity before fiscal 2028, but with a covenant test that tightens, definition risk around receivables, a shrinking top line and an earnings recovery driven by cost reductions and pricing while revenue and volume still decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Vestis is a standalone, publicly listed provider of uniform rental and workplace supplies in the United States and Canada, created by the spin-off from Aramark on September 30, 2023. The sources disclose no sponsor, and no parent or borrower distinct from the listed registrant is named in them; they show no leveraged buyout, acquisition or dividend recapitalisation in the period examined. The one transaction that defines the capital structure is the separation itself: the company borrowed under a new senior secured credit agreement and transferred roughly 1,457 million (US$) of proceeds to Aramark (10-K page:112). Since then the only financing changes are a refinancing of one term loan in February 2024, a covenant amendment in May 2025 that traded relief for restrictions on dividends, buybacks and receivables facilities, and a receivables securitization put in place in August 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model gives good revenue visibility: recurring weekly rental service under multi-year contracts is 95% of revenue, more than 300,000 accounts and no meaningful concentration (the ten largest customers are under 10% of revenue). The countervailing evidence is that revenue is nonetheless contracting: the nine-month decline in revenue and the quarter's lower volume are explained in part by a deliberate exit of unprofitable business under the transformation plan, and fiscal 2025 revenue included the loss of a national account customer. The mechanism matters for creditors: a recurring base protects against sudden revenue loss, but contract exit costs are modest relative to a service-quality failure, and the business has a high fixed cost base of plants and routes, so volume decline compresses operating leverage unless cost is removed at the same pace. This is why the earlier financial handoff shows earnings recovery driven by cost reduction and pricing rather than volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-relevant change is the transformation plan launched in the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Management targets annual cost savings of at least $75 million by the end of fiscal 2026 and has roughly $30 million realised through the third quarter (Q3 release page:2). These are management claims, not filed facts; the filed fact is that third-party consulting and severance costs have been incurred and that the estimated plan cost has been raised since the 10-K. Governance signals are mixed rather than adverse: no extraction-oriented behaviour is documented, dividends are suspended by the credit agreement amendment, but the principal financial officer role is filled on an interim basis and securities class actions allege misleading statements about pricing practices and outlook (allegations, not findings). Evidence quality is High for filed facts and Low for management claims on savings and market position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction history in the sources is the separation from Aramark and the financings around it; there is no sponsor transaction, acquisition or disposal of size, and no new debt issue in fiscal 2026 to the cutoff. On September 29, 2023 the company and certain subsidiaries entered into a senior secured credit agreement, and the separation was completed on September 30, 2023 by a distribution of Vestis shares to Aramark holders at one Vestis share for every two Aramark shares; the company used about 1,457 million of term loan proceeds to transfer cash to Aramark (10-K page:112, page:145). The agreement was amended on February 22, 2024 to refinance the original 800 million term loan A-1 with an 800 million term loan B-1 due February 2031, and on May 1, 2025 to raise the maximum net leverage ratio in stages, grant a one-time 15 million bad debt adjustment to covenant EBITDA, cap receivables facilities at 250 million and restrict dividends and share repurchases (10-K page:113, page:115). A three-year 250 million accounts receivable securitization was put in place on August 2, 2024 (10-K page:146). Use of proceeds on the securitization was repayment of part of the term loans (Q3 10-Q page:50). In fiscal 2026 the sources show only repayments of principal, with no new instrument. Liquidity effect and covenant terms are in the earlier financial handoff and are company-reported; the executed amendments are not supplied. The company also sold its equity stake in Aramark Uniform Services Japan Corporation in the first quarter of fiscal 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:15). Status of every item above: completed; none is draft or pending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Vestis is a leveraged but improving credit. Earnings and cash flow have recovered through fiscal 2026, and company-reported net leverage fell from 4.72x at October 3, 2025 to 4.10x at July 3, 2026, with liquidity of USD 351.8 million and no bank maturity before fiscal 2028. The strongest support is a recurring rental revenue base and USD 71.0 million of principal debt repaid since fiscal year end. The weakest point is that revenue and net volumes are still falling, so the recovery rests on a cost programme whose savings management, not the filings, has quantified. Two things decide the outcome: whether covenant EBITDA stays ahead of a maximum net leverage ratio that steps down from 5.00x to 4.75x and then 4.50x, and whether the receivables facility due August 2, 2027 is renewed or replaced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Vestis has reduced reported leverage on every measure while its top line has contracted. Company-reported net leverage moved from 4.72x at October 3, 2025 to 4.83x at January 2, 2026, 4.47x at April 3, 2026 and 4.10x at July 3, 2026, and the leverage on the financial handoff's basis (company Adjusted EBITDA, principal debt plus finance leases) moved from 5.19x to 4.33x for total debt and from 5.07x to 4.13x for net debt over the same dates [CP-1, Chart data: leverage]. The mechanism is both a smaller numerator (principal debt of USD 1,097.5 million at July 3, 2026 after repayments) and a larger denominator, because trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 257,425 thousand to USD 290,437 thousand. For creditors this is genuine progress, categorised as Documentary Fact for the reported ratios and Analyst Interpretation for the reading that it reflects operations rather than only repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The covenant cushion is adequate today and narrows on a known schedule. At July 3, 2026 the reported ratio of 4.10x sat 0.90x below the 5.00x maximum, equal to an EBITDA cushion of USD 52,961 thousand or 18.0% of covenant EBITDA; holding July 3, 2026 net debt constant, the same cushion falls to USD 40,272 thousand (13.7%) at 4.75x and USD 26,174 thousand (8.9%) at 4.50x [CP-1, Calculation steps]. Any shortfall in plan savings or a rise in net debt therefore bites first at the 4.50x test from the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The calculation is static and company-reported; it is not a forecast. The minimum interest cover covenant of 2.00x looks distant on an indicative basis (3.35x on covenant EBITDA over interest expense, net), but the executed definition is not supplied and the company does not print the ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is moderate: the revenue base is recurring but shrinking. About 95% of fiscal 2025 revenue was recurring rental under multi-year contracts, spread over more than 300,000 accounts with the ten largest customers under 10% of revenue [CP-1A, Company and operating model]. Against that, nine month revenue fell 1.9%, net volumes fell 2.0%, partly through a deliberate exit of unprofitable business, and fiscal 2025 included the loss of a national account [CP-1, Financial base view; CP-1A, Credit translations]. The mechanism is operating leverage: with a fixed plant and route network, falling volume compresses margin unless cost is removed at least as fast, so the recovery in earnings depends on the transformation plan and on pricing, both of which management reports as working through the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transformation plan carries the earnings case and is mostly a management claim. Management targets annual savings of at least USD 75 million by the end of fiscal 2026 and reports roughly USD 30 million realised through the third quarter, while the estimated plan cost has risen from a range of USD 25 million to USD 30 million in the 10-K to a range of USD 35 million to USD 40 million in the latest 10-Q [CP-1A, Conflicts and inherited items]. Category: Management Language for the savings, Documentary Fact for the cost estimate change. For creditors the implication is that covenant headroom is partly a function of adjustments and savings that have not been independently verified, and execution risk includes service disruption and customer attrition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and bank maturities are distant. Liquidity of USD 351.8 million at July 3, 2026 comprised USD 294.2 million of revolver availability and USD 57.7 million of cash, with no revolver borrowings; the term loans mature in fiscal 2028 (USD 436.0 million) and fiscal 2031 (USD 661.5 million) [CP-1, Chart data: liquidity and debt maturities]. The revolver commitment of USD 300 million also matures in September 2028, so the first bank refinancing is just under two years away, not immediate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The receivables securitization is the nearest funding event and a source of cash flow flattery. The USD 250 million facility is scheduled to terminate on August 2, 2027, and USD 212.3 million of receivables had been sold and derecognized at July 3, 2026, up USD 9.8 million since October 3, 2025 [CP-1, Calculation steps]. The mechanism is that the sold balance is not debt on the balance sheet; if the facility ended without replacement, receivables would return to the balance sheet and be funded from cash and the revolver, the credit agreement caps such facilities at USD 250 million, and the company's own net debt table does not include the sold balance. How the covenant counts the sold balance is unresolved: adding it to company net debt at July 3, 2026 gives 4.82x against the 5.00x maximum, and the same exercise at October 3, 2025 gives 5.45x, above the maximum then in force although the company reported compliance, which suggests the covenant does not count the whole balance on that basis. Category: Analyst Interpretation resting on an illustrative calculation, with the executed definition Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow quality improved but should be read with care. Nine month operating cash flow was USD 160,873 thousand against USD 33,302 thousand a year earlier, and trailing twelve month free cash flow of USD 136,411 thousand was 47.0% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1, Calculation steps]. Of the USD 127,571 thousand increase, the accepted financial handoff attributes USD 79.0 million to changes in operating assets and liabilities, while receivables sold rose by USD 9.8 million and USD 34,256 thousand of plan cash costs were absorbed in operating cash flow. Implication: free cash flow is real but includes working capital release that is unlikely to repeat at the same scale, and dividends and buybacks are restricted until conditions are met, so cash is going to debt service rather than shareholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance looks creditor-neutral with monitoring items. No sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or creditor-adverse action is documented, dividends are restricted, and the company reports its covenant ratio and liquidity each quarter; offsetting this, the chief financial officer role is interim, securities class actions alleging misleading disclosure are in discovery, and tax-free spin-off restrictions and indemnification obligations to Aramark remain unquantified [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Category: Documentary Fact for the events, Insufficient Information for the exposures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, recurring revenue and breadth: recurring weekly rental is about 95% of revenue, with no meaningful customer concentration, which supports revenue visibility and limits event risk [Documentary Fact, from the business handoff]. Second, deleveraging with real cash generation: principal debt is down USD 71.0 million since October 3, 2025 and trailing free cash flow of USD 136,411 thousand funded it, with the revolver undrawn [Documentary Fact for the debt and cash flow, from the financial handoff]. Third, liquidity and maturity profile: liquidity of USD 351.8 million and no bank maturity until fiscal 2028 give time to execute the plan [Documentary Fact]. Fourth, a single secured bank facility with no junior debt in the sources: all funded borrowings sit in one credit agreement (finance leases and the receivables facility sit alongside it) guaranteed by the company and substantially all wholly-owned domestic material subsidiaries and secured on substantially all tangible assets, which keeps the structure simple and the covenant package, once read in full, central to monitoring [Documentary Fact; legal capacity Not supplied]. Fifth, improving margins: trailing Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.8% against 9.4% for fiscal 2025 on the company's non-GAAP definition [Management Language, company-defined].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, leverage remains high and the covenant tightens: reported net leverage of 4.10x is below the 5.00x maximum, but the maximum falls to 4.50x from the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which leaves a smaller cushion at constant net debt [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the cushion]. Second, a shrinking top line: revenue down 1.9% and volume down 2.0% over nine months mean earnings recovery is cost-led [Documentary Fact]. Third, dependence on a management-quantified plan whose cost estimate has risen and whose savings are unaudited [Management Language]. Fourth, off-balance-sheet receivables funding with a defined end date and unresolved covenant treatment [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the covenant]. Fifth, definition risk: two company figures for fiscal 2025 Adjusted EBITDA differ, and covenant EBITDA includes adjustments the company defines [Documentary Fact]. Sixth, leadership and legal overhang: an interim chief financial officer and pending securities class actions [Documentary Fact; exposure Insufficient Information]. Seventh, supply chain concentration: about 60% of uniforms and linens are made in two plants in Mexico, with tariff sensitivity not quantified [Documentary Fact; sensitivity Insufficient Information].
